name: Somsri Lumsam
profile: Listed by Hurun Global (2018-2024) at ~US$1.2bn with CP Group as source of wealth. Searches found no person of this exact spelling linked to CP Group (owned by the Chearavanont family); a 'Somsri Lamsam' appears on a 2023 Thai rich list without a stated business link.
notes: Identity unresolved: the name is likely a romanisation of Somsri Lamsam (Lamsam family is associated with Kasikornbank/Muang Thai, not CP Group), so the Hurun CP Group attribution may be an error. Verify in Thai-language sources before any outreach. Caproasia 2023 list: https://www.caproasia.com/2023/04/15/2023-top-20-richest-in-thailand/

name: Jeremy Allaire
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Circle Internet Group (NYSE: CRCL)
profile: Serial entrepreneur who co-founded Allaire Corp. (ColdFusion; IPO 1999, sold to Macromedia) and Brightcove (online video, IPO 2012). Pivoted to crypto in 2013 co-founding Circle, issuer of the USDC stablecoin, and took it public in June 2025, the first IPO of a stablecoin issuer.
interesting_fact: He has now taken three companies public: Allaire Corp. (1999), Brightcove (2012) and Circle (2025).
deep_cut_fact: In 1994-96, fresh out of Macalester College (political science and philosophy), he worked with Noam Chomsky and his wife Carol to build the first comprehensive online archive of Chomsky's political writings.
notes: Very public and active on X (@jerallaire); regular podcast/conference guest on stablecoins and payments. Circle press office is the best route.

name: Arvind Nithrakashyap
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Rubrik, Inc. (NYSE: RBRK)
profile: IIT Madras (1995) and UMass Amherst (MS 1997) computer scientist who spent years at Oracle, where he co-founded the Exadata database platform, then led real-time ad infrastructure at Rocket Fuel. In 2013/14 he co-founded data-security company Rubrik, which IPO'd in 2024; his stake makes him a billionaire.
interesting_fact: At Oracle he co-founded Exadata, now one of Oracle's flagship database/storage platforms, before leaving to co-found Rubrik.
deep_cut_fact: At Rocket Fuel he architected the real-time bidding engine, leading ~30 engineers on an ad platform handling 50 billion requests a day at 50-60 ms latency; IIT Madras later gave him its Distinguished Alumnus Award.
notes: Low-profile technical founder but does keynotes/panels; route via Rubrik PR (Meghan Fintland, Head of Global PR, listed on releases).

name: Xiong Haitao
current_role: Actual controller of Gaojin Technology Industry Group (largest shareholder of Dongcai Technology, Gaomeng New Materials, Yichang Technology); vice chair of Dongcai Technology
profile: Chinese businesswoman, formerly a Kingfa Sci. & Tech. director (1998-May 2024) and ex-wife of Kingfa founder Yuan Zhimin; still a Kingfa shareholder (~1.5%). Through Gaojin Group she controls three Shanghai/Shenzhen-listed materials companies.
interesting_fact: Via Gaojin Technology Industry Group she is the ultimate controller of three separate A-share companies: Dongcai Technology (insulation/film materials), Gaomeng New Materials (adhesives) and Yichang Technology.
notes: Sensitive: in Jan 2026 the three listed companies announced she had been placed under detention (liuzhi) and investigation by the Sichuan Supervisory Commission; she resigned from Yichang's board 26 Jan 2026. Not a suitable outreach target at present. Source: https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202601273632524882.html

name: Wee Wei Ling
current_role: Executive Director (Sustainability Partnerships, Lifestyle & Asset), Pan Pacific Hotels Group; director, Kheng Leong and the Wee Foundation
profile: Eldest child of the late UOB patriarch Wee Cho Yaw. At UOL's Pan Pacific Hotels Group she oversees owned hotels, the St. Gregory spa and Si Chuan Dou Hua restaurant brands and the group's sustainability and community partnerships; she also sits on the family's Kheng Leong property firm and Wee Foundation boards.
interesting_fact: A champion of inclusive hiring, she has pushed companies to treat employing people with special needs as corporate strategy rather than charity, and chaired Project We Care, the People's Association's CEO network for corporate volunteerism, from 2011.
deep_cut_fact: She personally curated Pan Pacific's corporate art collection of local artists, published as the book 'Along the Journey', and co-founded the performing-arts charity Extra.Ordinary People with her cousin Wee Boo Kuan; she kept a Delia Prvacki ceramic bought in 1997 even after selling the hotel it was in.
notes: Gives lifestyle-press interviews (Peak, Prestige, Tatler, Sleeper) on sustainability and inclusive hiring; best route is Pan Pacific Hotels Group corporate communications (Singapore) via its Mynewsdesk newsroom.

name: Baron Hans Heinrich Thyssen-Bornemisza
profile: Swiss-based industrialist and art collector (Thyssen steel/industrial fortune), whose collection became Madrid's Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum. Died 27 April 2002 in Sant Feliu de Guíxols, Spain, aged 81.
interesting_fact: In 1993 Spain acquired the bulk of his art collection, now displayed at the Museo Nacional Thyssen-Bornemisza in Madrid.
notes: Deceased (2002). Name in input is misspelled 'Bornesmisza'. Only listed on Forbes 1996.

name: Pedro Brescia Moreyra
current_role: Co-Chairman, Grupo Breca (Peru); Vice Chairman, Rímac Seguros
profile: Third-generation member (born 1971, son of Mario Brescia Cafferata) of the family behind Breca, Peru's largest conglomerate (Minsur tin/copper mining, TASA fishmeal, Rímac insurance, BBVA Perú stake, Melón cement, real estate). Formerly Breca's general manager, he now co-chairs the group with cousin Alex Fort Brescia and sits on many group boards.
interesting_fact: Breca's mining arm Minsur is one of the world's largest tin producers and, through Marcobre, runs the Mina Justa copper project; Pedro sits on both boards.
deep_cut_fact: A Universidad de Lima business graduate with a Kellogg MBA, he serves on the board of Aporta (Breca's social-impact platform) and is a director of the Instituto Peruano de Economía think tank.
notes: Do not confuse with his uncle Pedro Brescia Cafferata (1921-2014). Family is very private; route via Breca corporate communications. Energy/mining angle (Minsur, Marcobre) fits the podcast.

name: Binny Bansal
current_role: Founder, OppDoor (Singapore) and co-founder/chairman, xto10x Technologies; invests via Three State Ventures
profile: IIT Delhi computer-science graduate from Chandigarh who co-founded Flipkart with Sachin Bansal in 2007 after a stint at Amazon, later serving as Flipkart CEO and group CEO before leaving in 2018. Now Singapore-based, he backs startups and runs OppDoor, a platform helping e-commerce brands expand into new markets.
interesting_fact: Before Flipkart he and Sachin Bansal first considered building a comparison-shopping search engine, but judged India's e-commerce market too small and started an online bookstore instead.
deep_cut_fact: Google rejected him twice before he joined Amazon as a software engineer in 2007; earlier he spent about 18 months at Sarnoff Corporation after IIT Delhi.
notes: Input spelling 'Bansaal' is a typo. Lives in Singapore; best route is LinkedIn or via OppDoor/xto10x. Avoid referencing his 2018 Flipkart exit.

name: George Feldstein
profile: Founder and chairman of Crestron Electronics, the AV and building-automation control company he started in 1969 in a room above a deli in New Jersey. Died 4 November 2014 (some sources say 5 Nov), aged 73; Crestron remains family-owned.
interesting_fact: He received both InfoComm's Adele de Berri Lifetime Achievement Award and CEDIA's Lifetime Achievement Award.
notes: Deceased (Nov 2014). Crestron is now run by his family; contact Crestron corporate communications if relevant.

name: Harshil Mathur
profile: IIT Roorkee graduate who co-founded Razorpay with batchmate Shashank Kumar in 2014 (Y Combinator-backed), building India's largest payment gateway by volume. Razorpay, valued at $7.5bn, now spans payments, banking, payroll and POS and is preparing for an Indian IPO.
interesting_fact: He has said nearly 100 banks rejected Razorpay before one agreed to partner, an early hurdle he credits with shaping the company.
deep_cut_fact: Razorpay began in 2014 as a social crowdfunding project 'to enable people to fund and help others in distress'; struggling to integrate payments, he and Kumar pivoted to payments. Before that he was a wireline field engineer at Schlumberger.
notes: Media-friendly and active on X/podcasts. Razorpay newsroom contact page (dated ~2021) also names individual comms staff.
